title: Continuous Batching & Paged Attention
summary: Continuous batching keeps GPUs busy by admitting new requests as others finish tokens. Paged attention makes the KV memory layout practical at high concurrency.

sections.title: From static to continuous batching
paragraphs: Static batching waits for an entire batch to finish before admitting new work — short requests pad behind long ones. Continuous (iteration-level) batching schedules at each decode step, so finished sequences free slots immediately.

The scheduler must account for KV memory, fairness, and latency SLOs. Without memory awareness, admitting too many sequences causes OOM; without fairness, long generations starve short interactive requests.

sections.title: Paged attention
paragraphs: Paged attention stores KV in non-contiguous blocks tracked by a block table, similar to OS virtual memory. This cuts waste from reserving max-context contiguous buffers per sequence and enables sharing blocks for identical prefixes.
